title: India sector analysis
intro: A practical map of the major Indian economy and listed-market sectors. Each card separates the present operating picture from the economic transmission, news drivers, SWOT and policy support.
disclaimer: This is a research snapshot, not a buy/sell call. Sector direction can change faster than this page; check the linked primary sources and company filings before acting.

sources.name: PM India · BHAVYA Rasayan chemical parks
PM India · 2026–27 capital expenditure and railways

sectors.name: Financial services
sectors.summary: Credit, savings, risk transfer and market intermediation remain central to domestic growth.

subsectors.name: Banks
subsectors.analysis: Credit demand is still supported by formalisation, housing, infrastructure and consumption, but the next leg depends on deposit growth, asset quality and the cost of funds rather than loan growth alone.
subsectors.impact: Banks transmit monetary policy into household EMIs, working capital and capex. Stronger credit can lift investment; weaker deposits or stressed borrowers can amplify a slowdown.
news: RBI policy stance and liquidity operations → funding costs and net interest margins
Quarterly slippages, credit costs and deposit competition → earnings quality
Public-sector bank capital and infrastructure-loan updates → system risk appetite

swot.strengths: Large, increasingly formal domestic customer base
swot.weaknesses: Deposit mobilisation and cycle-sensitive credit costs
swot.opportunities: MSME, housing, digital payments and capex financing
swot.threats: Asset-quality reversal, fraud and margin compression

policies.text: RBI prudential, digital-lending and payment-system rules
Public infrastructure and formalisation priorities

subsectors.name: NBFCs and housing finance
subsectors.analysis: Specialist lenders retain an edge in underserved retail, vehicle, microfinance and property-linked credit. The trade-off is higher sensitivity to wholesale funding, collections and regulatory tightening.
subsectors.impact: NBFCs widen credit access for households and small businesses, especially where banks lack distribution. A funding shock can quickly reduce consumption and construction activity.
news: Borrowing spreads, securitisation volumes and bond-market liquidity
Microfinance collections and rural cash flows
Housing sales, property prices and affordable-housing demand

swot.strengths: Specialist underwriting and last-mile distribution
swot.opportunities: Affordable housing, vehicle finance and MSME formalisation
swot.threats: Liquidity stress, collection weakness and tighter norms

policies.text: Housing, financial-inclusion and digital-credit frameworks

subsectors.name: Insurance
subsectors.analysis: Low penetration, rising protection awareness and formal employment support a long runway. Near-term profitability still varies sharply by product mix, distribution cost and claims inflation.
subsectors.impact: Insurance converts household and business risks into investible long-term pools, supporting capital formation while improving resilience after health, crop or catastrophe losses.
news: IRDAI product, commission and foreign-investment decisions
Health and motor claims inflation
Life premium growth, persistency and solvency ratios

swot.strengths: Under-penetrated market with recurring premium pools
swot.weaknesses: Complex products and high distribution costs
swot.opportunities: Health, term life, crop and embedded insurance
swot.threats: Mis-selling, catastrophe losses and claims inflation

policies.text: Insurance-penetration and financial-inclusion reforms

subsectors.name: Capital markets and fintech
subsectors.analysis: Retail participation, SIPs, demat accounts and digital rails have deepened market access. Valuations and revenue quality deserve more attention as trading activity normalises and compliance costs rise.
subsectors.impact: Efficient markets lower the cost of capital for companies and give households more ways to save. Excess leverage or speculative activity can increase household losses and volatility.
news: SEBI market-structure, derivatives and investor-protection changes
Mutual-fund flows, SIP growth and IPO pipeline
UPI, account-aggregator and fraud-prevention adoption

swot.strengths: World-scale digital public infrastructure
swot.opportunities: Wealth management, pensions and transparent fintech
swot.threats: Cyber incidents, regulatory compression and market sell-offs

policies.text: Digital public infrastructure and investor-protection reforms

sectors.name: IT, digital and communications
sectors.summary: Export services are moving from labour arbitrage towards AI-enabled transformation and owned platforms.

subsectors.name: IT services and GCCs
subsectors.analysis: Demand is bifurcated: cost takeout and cloud/AI work remain resilient, while discretionary transformation budgets and traditional application work are more uneven. Currency and utilisation matter for margins.
subsectors.impact: IT exports bring foreign exchange, high-value jobs and productivity gains to client economies. A global tech-spending slowdown can affect urban employment, office demand and services exports.
news: US and European tech budgets, deal wins and vendor consolidation
Generative-AI productivity claims versus billing and headcount
GCC announcements, hiring and campus expansion

swot.strengths: Deep talent pool, scale and global delivery
swot.weaknesses: Concentration in a few geographies and large clients
swot.opportunities: AI engineering, cybersecurity and vertical platforms
swot.threats: Automation, pricing pressure and visa/geopolitical risk

policies.text: IndiaAI, skilling and digital-infrastructure initiatives

subsectors.name: Software, AI and cybersecurity
subsectors.analysis: AI adoption is expanding demand for compute, data engineering, model governance and security, but monetisation is still being tested. Winners should pair proprietary data or workflow depth with lower inference costs.
subsectors.impact: Productivity gains can lift output without proportional labour growth, while cyber resilience reduces disruption across banks, hospitals, factories and government systems.
news: Model releases, enterprise AI budgets and data-centre capacity
IndiaAI compute and sovereign-model announcements
Cyber breaches, privacy enforcement and responsible-AI rules

swot.strengths: Large engineering base and digital adoption
swot.opportunities: Vertical AI, public digital rails and cyber defence
swot.threats: Fast obsolescence, compute cost and data regulation

policies.text: IndiaAI Mission and semiconductor ecosystem support

subsectors.name: Telecom and data centres
subsectors.analysis: Data usage, 5G monetisation and cloud demand support capex, but the sector remains capital-intensive with high spectrum, energy and right-of-way costs. Consolidation has improved pricing discipline.
subsectors.impact: Connectivity lowers transaction costs and enables digital services, remote work and financial inclusion. Data-centre build-out also creates demand for power, cooling, construction and network equipment.
news: Tariff revisions, 5G enterprise use cases and spectrum policy
Data-centre leases, power availability and AI-compute demand
Right-of-way, cybersecurity and data-localisation rules

swot.strengths: Large data market and improving network scale
swot.opportunities: Fibre, edge compute, private 5G and cloud
swot.threats: Price wars, energy constraints and cyber outages

policies.text: Digital India, data infrastructure and electronics policy
Capital-investment focus on enabling infrastructure

sectors.name: Industrials and infrastructure
sectors.summary: Public capex, private manufacturing and logistics upgrades are creating a multi-year order-cycle, with execution as the key filter.

subsectors.name: Capital goods and EPC
subsectors.analysis: Order books benefit from power, rail, defence, factory and urban-infrastructure spending. The healthier businesses are those converting orders into cash without stretching working capital.
subsectors.impact: Capital formation raises productivity and creates upstream demand for metals, engineering, logistics and skilled labour. Delays can lock up capital and reduce the multiplier.
news: Fresh order awards, execution milestones and working-capital days
Private capex intentions and capacity-utilisation data
Commodity, freight and project-finance costs

swot.strengths: Domestic demand and technical capability
swot.opportunities: Factory build-out, grid, rail and exports
swot.threats: Cost overruns, cancellations and commodity spikes

policies.text: Capital-expenditure and manufacturing push
PLI and strategic manufacturing support

subsectors.name: Roads, rail, ports and logistics
subsectors.analysis: Multimodal connectivity and freight capacity remain strong structural themes. Financial performance depends on traffic, concession terms, land availability and whether public projects are awarded and executed on time.
subsectors.impact: Lower logistics costs improve the competitiveness of farms, factories and exporters; construction also supports employment and regional development.
news: Road awards, toll growth, rail capex and dedicated freight corridors
Port volumes, shipping rates and container availability
Land acquisition, environmental clearances and state execution

swot.strengths: Large infrastructure gap and policy priority
swot.opportunities: Freight, warehousing, airports and urban transit
swot.threats: Delays, leverage and traffic underperformance

policies.text: National logistics and integrated infrastructure priorities
Modified UDAN for regional aviation connectivity

subsectors.name: Cement and building materials
subsectors.analysis: Demand tracks housing, roads and industrial construction. Volume growth can be healthy while margins remain sensitive to coal, petcoke, freight, regional oversupply and consolidation.
subsectors.impact: Construction materials are a direct bridge from public/private capex to jobs and fixed-asset creation, but price competition affects contractor and developer viability.
news: Cement dispatches, realisations and capacity additions
Coal/petcoke, freight and electricity costs
Housing launches, road awards and monsoon-led construction pace

swot.strengths: Essential local product with pricing power in tight markets
swot.weaknesses: Energy intensity and regional freight economics
swot.opportunities: Urbanisation, premium products and consolidation
swot.threats: Oversupply, carbon costs and weak real estate

policies.text: Public capex, housing and infrastructure pipeline

sectors.name: Automobiles and mobility
sectors.summary: Demand is broadening beyond passenger cars as two-wheelers, commercial vehicles and electric mobility compete on affordability and total cost.

subsectors.name: Passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and commercial vehicles
subsectors.analysis: Urban income, rural recovery, replacement demand and financing costs drive volumes. Premiumisation helps margins, but entry-level affordability and fleet utilisation remain important stress points.
subsectors.impact: Auto creates a large manufacturing and services ecosystem, from steel and components to finance, fuel, repair and logistics.
news: Monthly registrations, discounts, inventory and rural demand
Fuel prices, interest rates and vehicle-finance approvals
Emission/safety norms, scrappage and export demand

swot.strengths: Large domestic market and supplier depth
swot.opportunities: Premiumisation, exports and platform sharing
swot.threats: Input inflation, regulation and demand slowdown

policies.text: Auto and component PLI, scrappage and localisation measures

subsectors.name: EVs, batteries and charging
subsectors.analysis: Electric two-wheelers, buses and fleet use cases have a clearer economic case than every private-car segment. Scale, battery prices, residual values, charging uptime and subsidy continuity will decide adoption quality.
subsectors.impact: EVs can reduce oil dependence and local pollution while shifting value towards batteries, power electronics, software and grid services.
news: EV registrations, incentive rules and localisation content
Battery-cell capacity, mineral prices and safety recalls
Charging-network utilisation, fleet tenders and grid connections

swot.strengths: Lower running cost and policy-backed transition
swot.weaknesses: Charging, battery lifecycle and initial cost
swot.opportunities: Buses, delivery fleets, storage and exports
swot.threats: Subsidy changes, raw-material concentration and safety events

policies.text: PLI for advanced chemistry cells and auto components
Rare-earth and domestic supply-chain support

subsectors.name: Auto components
subsectors.analysis: Component makers gain from premiumisation, electronics content, exports and platform localisation. The transition raises addressable content but also requires capex, software capability and quality assurance.
subsectors.impact: The supplier base spreads manufacturing employment and export earnings across regions; localisation reduces import leakage but increases the need for skills and standards.
news: OEM production plans, localisation awards and export orders
Semiconductor availability and raw-material prices
EV content, ADAS adoption and quality recalls

swot.strengths: Established supplier clusters and export capability
swot.weaknesses: OEM bargaining power and capex needs
swot.opportunities: EV, electronics, precision and global sourcing
swot.threats: Technology displacement and customer concentration

policies.text: PLI for auto and advanced automotive technology
Semiconductor and electronics ecosystem support

sectors.name: Energy and utilities
sectors.summary: India needs more reliable, affordable power while simultaneously reducing import dependence and carbon intensity.

subsectors.name: Oil, gas and refining
subsectors.analysis: Refiners and gas distributors balance domestic demand with crude differentials, shipping, currency and administered pricing. Energy security remains a policy priority, but transition risk changes long-duration valuations.
subsectors.impact: Energy prices flow through transport, fertiliser, chemicals, inflation and household budgets. Supply disruptions can widen the current-account deficit and slow growth.
news: Crude and gas prices, OPEC+ decisions and shipping disruption
Refining margins, fuel pricing and inventory gains/losses
Gas allocation, city-gas volumes and import dependence

swot.strengths: Large demand base and integrated refining assets
swot.opportunities: Petrochemicals, gas penetration and cleaner fuels
swot.threats: Geopolitics, transition policy and stranded assets

policies.text: Energy-security, gas-market and strategic manufacturing measures

subsectors.name: Power generation and distribution
subsectors.analysis: Load growth from manufacturing, cooling, rail and data centres supports generation and grid investment. The investability of distribution still depends on tariffs, losses, payment discipline and state reform.
subsectors.impact: Reliable electricity is an economy-wide input: it raises factory utilisation, supports digital infrastructure and reduces the productivity cost of outages.
news: Peak demand, power-market prices and fuel availability
DISCOM dues, tariff orders and loss-reduction progress
Transmission tenders, storage and grid-balancing needs

swot.strengths: Structural demand and essential-service status
swot.opportunities: Transmission, smart meters and storage
swot.threats: Regulatory lag, heatwaves and coal/import volatility

policies.text: Grid, rail and national infrastructure capex
Renewable-purchase and energy-storage obligations

subsectors.name: Renewables, storage and green hydrogen
subsectors.analysis: Solar and wind deployment are moving from project growth to system integration: transmission, firm power, batteries, domestic modules and bankable offtake are the bottlenecks to watch.
subsectors.impact: Cleaner domestic energy can reduce fuel imports, improve energy security and create new manufacturing chains, though land, water, transmission and financing remain real constraints.
news: Auction tariffs, module prices, curtailment and transmission readiness
Battery-storage tenders, round-the-clock power and grid rules
Green-hydrogen offtake, electrolyser awards and export corridors

swot.strengths: Falling technology costs and strong policy intent
swot.opportunities: Storage, green molecules, manufacturing and exports
swot.threats: Module oversupply, policy changes and financing stress

policies.text: National Green Hydrogen Mission and SIGHT incentives
Renewable-energy and storage procurement framework

sectors.name: Healthcare and life sciences
sectors.summary: Demand is structurally defensive, but the earnings mix spans low-margin generics, high-risk innovation and capacity-constrained care delivery.

subsectors.name: Generics, APIs and formulations
subsectors.analysis: India remains important to global generic supply, while domestic branded generics benefit from rising healthcare spend. US pricing, inspections, compliance and input costs separate durable franchises from volume-only businesses.
subsectors.impact: Affordable medicines support labour productivity and reduce household financial shocks; exports bring services and manufacturing value to the economy.
news: USFDA observations, product launches and pricing pressure
API costs, China supply and domestic medicine demand
Pharmacy-channel consolidation and government procurement

swot.strengths: Scale, chemistry talent and global manufacturing base
swot.opportunities: Complex generics, biosimilars and emerging markets
swot.threats: Plant observations, litigation and supply disruptions

policies.text: Pharma PLI, bulk-drug parks and manufacturing support

subsectors.name: Biopharma and CDMO
subsectors.analysis: Biologics, biosimilars, clinical research and outsourced manufacturing offer higher value than commodity volume, but require patient capital, quality systems and scientific talent.
subsectors.impact: A stronger biopharma base improves health security, creates high-skill employment and can attract global R&D and manufacturing investment.
news: Clinical readouts, licensing and biosimilar approvals
Global biotech funding and CDMO utilisation
Regulatory review timelines and manufacturing inspections

swot.strengths: Scientific talent and cost-efficient manufacturing
swot.weaknesses: Long development cycles and quality intensity
swot.opportunities: Biosimilars, vaccines, clinical trials and exports
swot.threats: Trial failures, IP disputes and compliance events

policies.text: Biopharma SHAKTI, NIPER and clinical-trial ecosystem

subsectors.name: Hospitals, diagnostics and medtech
subsectors.analysis: Urban capacity expansion, insurance coverage and chronic-disease prevalence support demand. Execution risks include doctor availability, price regulation, payer mix and the capex needed outside major cities.
subsectors.impact: Healthcare capacity raises human capital and reduces travel/time losses for families; it also creates formal jobs and demand for devices, diagnostics and pharmaceuticals.
news: Occupancy, ARPOB, procedure mix and new-bed additions
Insurance claims, package rates and medical inflation
Device approvals, imports and domestic medtech capacity

swot.strengths: Under-supplied care and recurring demand
swot.opportunities: Tier-II cities, diagnostics, day-care and medtech
swot.threats: Price caps, clinical risk and talent shortages

policies.text: Biopharma and healthcare-capacity push

sectors.name: Consumer and retail
sectors.summary: The long-term opportunity is formalisation and premiumisation; the near-term read comes from rural demand, food inflation and competitive intensity.

subsectors.name: FMCG and household products
subsectors.analysis: Volume growth is healthier when food inflation eases and rural incomes improve. Premium categories can defend margins, while commodity spikes and down-trading pressure mass products.
subsectors.impact: Consumer demand is a major growth engine and a fast read on household purchasing power, wages and inflation expectations.
news: Rural wages, monsoon/harvest outcomes and distributor inventory
Palm oil, crude derivatives, packaging and agri-commodity prices
GST, quick-commerce and private-label competition

swot.strengths: Distribution, brands and recurring consumption
swot.weaknesses: Input sensitivity and mature urban categories
swot.opportunities: Rural penetration, premiumisation and health products
swot.threats: Down-trading, private labels and commodity inflation

policies.text: Rural income, food supply and formal-retail infrastructure measures

subsectors.name: Retail and e-commerce
subsectors.analysis: Organised retail continues to take share through convenience, assortment and formal payments. Profitability varies by rent, fulfilment density, discounting and customer acquisition cost.
subsectors.impact: Formal retail creates jobs, widens market access for brands and improves tax/documentation trails, but can displace fragmented sellers and increase packaging/logistics demand.
news: Same-store sales, footfalls, GMV and festive-season trends
Quick-commerce dark-store economics and delivery costs
E-commerce, data, FDI and consumer-protection rules

swot.strengths: Scale, data and improving logistics
swot.weaknesses: Thin margins and high customer-acquisition cost
swot.opportunities: Tier-II/III cities, private labels and omnichannel
swot.threats: Discount wars, regulation and demand volatility

policies.text: Digital payments, logistics and consumer-market formalisation

subsectors.name: Consumer durables and appliances
subsectors.analysis: Cooling, electrification, housing formation and replacement demand support appliances. Energy efficiency, input costs, channel inventory and summer weather can make quarterly performance lumpy.
subsectors.impact: Durables improve household productivity and create demand for electronics, plastics, metals, logistics and service networks.
news: Weather, housing completions and financing availability
Copper, steel, plastics and compressor costs
Energy-efficiency labels, import duties and local manufacturing

swot.strengths: Low penetration and aspirational demand
swot.opportunities: Cooling, premium products and localisation
swot.threats: Input spikes, weak incomes and aggressive discounting

policies.text: Electronics components and manufacturing localisation

sectors.name: Agriculture and food
sectors.summary: Agriculture remains a large employment and demand base; productivity, water, storage and processing determine how much value reaches producers.

subsectors.name: Farm inputs and agri-services
subsectors.analysis: Seed, fertiliser, crop-protection and precision-farming demand follows acreage, farm profitability, weather and subsidy design. Regulation and raw-material imports can change margins quickly.
subsectors.impact: Better yields and input efficiency support rural income, food security and lower food inflation; poor seasons reduce consumption and increase fiscal pressure.
news: Monsoon, reservoir levels, sowing and crop-health indicators
Fertiliser availability, subsidy payments and input prices
AgriStack, crop-insurance claims and digital marketplaces

swot.strengths: Large addressable farm base and recurring need
swot.opportunities: Micro-irrigation, precision and biological inputs
swot.threats: Climate shocks, counterfeit inputs and price controls

policies.text: AgriStack, irrigation, crop insurance and farm-support programmes

subsectors.name: Food processing and cold chain
subsectors.analysis: Processing gains from changing diets, organised retail and export standards. Capacity utilisation and procurement matter more than headline installed capacity, especially in perishables.
subsectors.impact: Processing reduces wastage, extends shelf life, creates non-farm jobs and improves farmer realisation by moving value up the chain.
news: Food inflation, procurement prices and export restrictions
Cold-storage utilisation, logistics and quality compliance
Packaged-food launches and private-label competition

swot.strengths: Large raw-material base and rising convenience demand
swot.opportunities: Value-added foods, exports and traceability
swot.threats: Food-safety events, climate volatility and input inflation

policies.text: Food-processing, logistics and storage incentives
Integrated infrastructure and cold-chain build-out

subsectors.name: Dairy, fisheries and livestock
subsectors.analysis: Demand is relatively resilient but margins are exposed to feed, disease, procurement prices and weather. Scale, cold chain, genetics and formal distribution are the main productivity levers.
subsectors.impact: Allied activities diversify rural income and contribute to nutrition, women’s employment and local value addition.
news: Milk procurement, feed costs and disease outbreaks
Aquaculture export demand and seafood compliance
Dairy prices, cooperative volumes and cold-chain investment

swot.strengths: Daily-consumption demand and rural reach
swot.opportunities: Value-added products, exports and formalisation
swot.threats: Disease, feed inflation and climate stress

policies.text: Food-processing, animal husbandry and cold-chain support

sectors.name: Materials, chemicals and textiles
sectors.summary: These export- and commodity-linked industries sit at the base of many value chains, so cycle, energy, trade and environmental rules matter together.

subsectors.name: Specialty chemicals and petrochemicals
subsectors.analysis: The medium-term case is import substitution and global supply-chain diversification, while the current cycle is shaped by China capacity, destocking, energy and customer inventory.
subsectors.impact: Chemicals raise value added across pharma, agriculture, auto, electronics and construction; environmental failures impose costs well beyond the plant.
news: Global chemical prices, Chinese operating rates and destocking
New capacities, customer qualification and export orders
Environmental clearances, carbon rules and feedstock costs

swot.strengths: Chemistry talent and growing domestic downstream demand
swot.opportunities: Specialty, electronic and sustainable chemicals
swot.threats: Oversupply, compliance events and trade barriers

policies.text: BHAVYA Rasayan chemical-park infrastructure
Import-substitution and strategic manufacturing support

subsectors.name: Steel, aluminium and mining
subsectors.analysis: Infrastructure and auto demand support volumes, but prices remain global and capital intensive. Domestic ore security helps, while energy, coking coal and trade flows drive margins.
subsectors.impact: Metals are foundational inputs for housing, transport, machinery and defence. Their prices feed into capex costs and inflation across the economy.
news: China output, global prices and safeguard/anti-dumping actions
Coking coal, power and freight costs
Mining auctions, environmental approvals and domestic demand

swot.strengths: Strategic domestic demand and scale players
swot.opportunities: Value-added alloys, recycling and exports
swot.threats: Global oversupply, carbon costs and import competition

policies.text: Infrastructure and manufacturing-led demand
Rare-earth corridors and critical-mineral supply-chain support

subsectors.name: Textiles and apparel
subsectors.analysis: India can gain from supply-chain diversification and technical textiles, but competitiveness depends on scale, lead times, labour productivity, power cost and trade access.
subsectors.impact: Textiles are labour-intensive and geographically distributed, making them important for women’s employment, exports and formal manufacturing jobs.
news: US/EU orders, cotton and man-made-fibre prices
Export duties, FTAs and sustainability traceability
Factory utilisation, wage costs and buyer destocking

swot.strengths: Raw-material base, design and labour pool
swot.opportunities: Technical textiles, MMF and supply-chain shifts
swot.threats: Bangladesh/Vietnam competition, tariffs and weak orders

policies.text: Textile PLI, PM MITRA parks and manufacturing support

sectors.name: Defence, aerospace and space
sectors.summary: Indigenisation is moving from procurement rhetoric towards platforms, components and exportable capability, though delivery timelines remain long.

subsectors.name: Defence manufacturing and electronics
subsectors.analysis: Domestic procurement, positive-indigenisation lists and electronics content improve the addressable market. The key checks are order conversion, certification, execution and customer concentration.
subsectors.impact: Defence production supports high-skill manufacturing, technology spillovers and strategic autonomy while reducing import leakage.
news: Acceptance-of-necessity, contract awards and delivery milestones
Indigenisation lists, export licences and geopolitical demand
Radar, drone, missile and semiconductor supply-chain developments

swot.strengths: Sovereign demand and engineering capability
swot.weaknesses: Long sales cycles and programme concentration
swot.opportunities: Electronics, drones, exports and maintenance
swot.threats: Procurement delays, cost overruns and geopolitics

policies.text: DAP 2026 and higher indigenous-content focus
Defence and strategic electronics manufacturing support

subsectors.name: Civil aviation and aerospace
subsectors.analysis: Passenger growth and regional connectivity support airports, airlines, MRO and component makers. Execution, aircraft availability, fuel cost and airport economics remain the operating variables.
subsectors.impact: Aviation compresses travel time, supports tourism and trade, and creates a cluster of high-value services and engineering work.
news: Passenger traffic, load factors, fares and jet-fuel prices
Aircraft deliveries, airport capex and MRO contracts
Regional routes and airline financial health

swot.strengths: Fast-growing travel demand and a young market
swot.opportunities: MRO, regional airports and aerospace components
swot.threats: Safety events, high fuel and airline distress

policies.text: Modified UDAN and regional airport development
Aerospace-component and strategic manufacturing support

subsectors.name: Space and launch services
subsectors.analysis: Commercial launch, satellite communications, earth observation and downstream applications are opening beyond the traditional public-sector model. Business quality depends on contracts, reliability and financing.
subsectors.impact: Space capability supports communications, navigation, weather, agriculture and national security, with spillovers into electronics and advanced manufacturing.
news: Launch cadence, satellite orders and private-sector approvals
Spectrum, space-regulation and insurance developments
Earth-observation, broadband and defence contracts

swot.strengths: Cost-efficient engineering and established launch capability
swot.weaknesses: Small commercial base and long qualification cycles
swot.opportunities: Satcom, launch, geospatial and defence applications
swot.threats: Launch failure, capital intensity and regulatory delay

policies.text: Strategic electronics, semiconductor and deep-tech support

sectors.name: Real estate, hospitality and urban services
sectors.summary: Housing, offices, warehouses and travel are linked to incomes, credit, migration and infrastructure; affordability is as important as headline sales.

subsectors.name: Residential real estate
subsectors.analysis: Premium and branded developers are seeing stronger formal demand, but affordability and interest rates limit the breadth of the cycle. Track collections, launches, inventory and project completion rather than bookings alone.
subsectors.impact: Housing drives cement, steel, appliances, finance and local employment; excessive leverage or unaffordable prices can crowd out consumption.
news: Sales, launches, unsold inventory and mortgage rates
Land approvals, RERA compliance and project completion
Income growth, migration and infrastructure connectivity

swot.strengths: Urban household formation and formalisation
swot.weaknesses: Capital intensity, land and execution risk
swot.opportunities: Affordable housing, rentals and tier-II cities
swot.threats: Rates, oversupply and regulatory delay

policies.text: Infrastructure connectivity and housing support

subsectors.name: Commercial real estate and warehousing
subsectors.analysis: GCCs, data centres, organised retail and manufacturing are supporting quality-office and logistics demand. Vacancy, tenant concentration and capex discipline decide returns.
subsectors.impact: Commercial space enables services exports and supply-chain efficiency, while construction creates jobs and demand for materials.
news: Office leasing, GCC expansion and vacancy
Warehouse absorption, e-commerce and manufacturing projects
Interest rates, REIT distributions and green-building rules

swot.strengths: Services, logistics and formalisation demand
swot.opportunities: Data centres, warehousing and REITs
swot.threats: Remote work, oversupply and high financing cost

policies.text: Digital infrastructure, logistics and manufacturing expansion

subsectors.name: Hotels, travel and tourism
subsectors.analysis: Domestic leisure, business travel and better connectivity support occupancy and room rates. Supply additions, airline capacity and consumer confidence create the next quarterly swing factor.
subsectors.impact: Tourism generates jobs and foreign exchange across hotels, transport, food, retail and local services, especially outside large cities.
news: Occupancy, ADR, airline capacity and travel bookings
Visa rules, destination events and regional connectivity
Fuel, wages and new-room supply

swot.strengths: Large domestic travel base and under-supplied destinations
swot.opportunities: Tier-II tourism, MICE and premium stays
swot.threats: Geopolitical shocks, weather and new supply

policies.text: Modified UDAN and tourism/infrastructure connectivity
